vsm2.14:211.0: D. Classes of Knowledge of the Aggregates
vsm2.14:211.1:
Having understood this, again as regards these same aggregates: Knowledge of aggregates is classed (1) As to order, and (2)
distinction, (3) As to neither less nor more, (4) And likewise as to simile, (5) And twice as to how to be seen,
(6) And as to good for one seeing thus— This is the way of exposition That a wise man should rightly know.
vsm2.14:211.2:
211. 1. Herein, as to order: order is of several kinds, namely, order of arising,
order of abandoning, order of practice, order of plane, order of teaching.
vsm2.14:211.3:
Herein, "First there comes to be the foetus in the first stage, then there
comes to be the foetus in the second stage" (S I 206), etc., is order of arising.
vsm2.14:211.4: "Things to be abandoned by seeing, things to be abandoned by development" (Dhs 1), etc., is order of abandoning.
vsm2.14:211.5: "Purification of virtue … purification of consciousness" (M I 148), etc., is order of practice.
vsm2.14:211.6: "The sense sphere, the fine-material sphere" (Paṭis I 83), etc., is order of plane.
vsm2.14:211.7:
"The four foundations of mindfulness, the four right efforts" (D II 120), etc., or "Talk on giving,
talk on virtue" (M I 379), etc., is order of teaching.
vsm2.14:212.1:
212. Of these, firstly, order of arising is not applicable here because the aggregates do not arise in the order in which they
are successively dealt with, as is the case with "the foetus in the first stage," etc.,
vsm2.14:212.2: nor is order of abandoning applicable, because the profitable and indeterminate are not to be abandoned;
vsm2.14:212.3: nor is order of practice, because what is unprofitable is not to be practiced;
vsm2.14:212.4: nor is order of plane, because feeling, etc., are included in all four planes.
vsm2.14:213.1: 213. Order of teaching is appropriate however;
vsm2.14:213.2:
for there are those people who, while teachable, have fallen into assuming a self among the five aggregates owing to failure
to analyze them; and the Blessed One is desirous of releasing them from the assumption by getting them to see how the seeming
compactness of mass in the five aggregates is resolved; and being desirous of their welfare, he first, for the purpose of their easy
apprehension, taught the materiality aggregate, which is gross, being the objective field of the eye, etc.;
vsm2.14:213.3: and after that, feeling, which feels matter as desirable and undesirable;
vsm2.14:213.4: then perception, which apprehends the aspects of feeling's objective field, since "What one feels, that one perceives" (M I 293);
vsm2.14:213.5: then formations, which form volitionally through the means of perception;
vsm2.14:213.6: and lastly, consciousness, which these things beginning with feeling have as their support, and which dominates them.
vsm2.14:213.7: This, in the first place, is how the exposition should be known as to order.
vsm2.14:214.1: 214. 2. As to distinction: as to the distinction between aggregates and aggregates-as-objects-of-clinging.
vsm2.14:214.2: But what is the distinction between them? Firstly, aggregates is said without distinguishing.
vsm2.14:214.3: Aggregates as objects of clinging is said distinguishing those that are subject to cankers and are liable to the clingings,
vsm2.14:214.4:
according as it is said: "Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the five aggregates and the five aggregates as objects of clinging.
Listen … And what, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates? Any kind of materiality whatever, bhikkhus, whether past, future or present
… far or near: this is called the materiality aggregate. Any kind of feeling whatever … Any kind of perception whatever … Any
kind of formations whatever … Any kind of consciousness whatever … far or near: this is called the consciousness aggregate.
These, bhikkhus, are called the five aggregates. And what, bhikkhus, are the five aggregates as objects of clinging? Any
kind of materiality whatever … far or near, that is subject to cankers and liable to the clingings: this is called the materiality
aggregate as object of clinging. Any kind of feeling whatever … Any kind of perception whatever … Any kind of formations whatever
… Any kind of consciousness whatever … far or near, that is subject to cankers and liable to the clingings: this is called the
consciousness aggregate as object of clinging. These, bhikkhus, are called the five aggregates as objects of clinging" (S III 47).
vsm2.14:215.1: 215. Now, while there is feeling, etc., both free from cankers and subject to them, not so materiality.
vsm2.14:215.2:
However, since materiality can be described as a simple aggregate in the sense of a total,
it is therefore mentioned among the simple aggregates.
vsm2.14:215.3:
And since it can be described as an aggregate that is the object of clinging in the sense of a total and in the sense
of being subjected to cankers, that same materiality is therefore mentioned among the aggregates as objects of clinging too.
vsm2.14:215.4:
But feeling, etc., are only mentioned among the simple aggregates when they are free from cankers.
When they are subject to cankers, they are mentioned among the aggregates as objects of clinging.
vsm2.14:215.5:
And here the meaning of the term "aggregates as objects of clinging" should be regarded as this:
aggregates that are the resort of clinging are aggregates of clinging.
vsm2.14:215.6: But here all these taken together are intended as aggregates.
vsm2.14:216.1: 216. 3. As to neither less nor more: but why are five aggregates, neither less nor more, mentioned by the Blessed One?
vsm2.14:216.2:
(a) Because all formed things that resemble each other fall into these groups, (b) because that is the widest limit as the basis
for the assumption of self and what pertains to self, and (c) because of the inclusion by them of the other sorts of aggregates.
vsm2.14:217.1:
217. (a) When the numerous categories of formed states are grouped together according to similarity, materiality
forms one aggregate through being grouped together according to similarity consisting in materiality;
vsm2.14:217.2: feeling forms one aggregate through being grouped together according to similarity consisting in feeling;
vsm2.14:217.3: and so with perception and the other two.
vsm2.14:217.4: So they are stated as five because similar formed things fall into groups.
vsm2.14:218.1:
218. (b) And this is the extreme limit as the basis for the assumption of self and what
pertains to self, that is to say, the five beginning with materiality.
vsm2.14:218.2:
For this is said: "Bhikkhus, when matter exists, it is through clinging to matter, through insisting upon (interpreting) matter,
that such a view as this arises: 'This is mine, this is I, this is my self.' When feeling exists … When perception exists … When
formations exist … When consciousness exists, it is through clinging to consciousness, through insisting upon (interpreting)
consciousness, that such a view as this arises: 'This is mine, this is I, this is my self'"(S III 181–82).
vsm2.14:218.3: So they are stated as five because this is the widest limit as a basis for the assumption of self and what pertains to self.
vsm2.14:219.1:
219. (c) And also, since those other sorts of aggregates stated as the five aggregates of things
beginning with virtue are comprised within the formations aggregate, they are included here too.
vsm2.14:219.2: Therefore they are stated as five because they include the other sorts.
vsm2.14:219.3: This is how the exposition should be known as to neither less nor more.
vsm2.14:220.1:
220. 4. As to simile: the materiality aggregate as object of clinging is like a sick-room because it is the dwelling-place,
as physical basis, door, and object, of the sick man, namely, the consciousness aggregate as object of clinging.
vsm2.14:220.2: The feeling aggregate as object of clinging is like the sickness because it afflicts.
vsm2.14:220.3:
The perception aggregate as object of clinging is like the provocation of the sickness because it gives
rise to feeling associated with greed, etc., owing to perception of sense desires, and so on.
vsm2.14:220.4:
The formations aggregate as object of clinging is like having recourse to what is unsuitable
because it is the source of feeling, which is the sickness;
vsm2.14:220.5: for it is said: "Feeling as feeling is the formed that they form" (S III 87),
vsm2.14:220.6:
and likewise: "Because of unprofitable kamma having been performed and stored up,
resultant body-consciousness has arisen accompanied by pain" (Dhs §556).
vsm2.14:220.7: The consciousness aggregate as object of clinging is like the sick man because it is never free from feeling, which is the sickness.
vsm2.14:221.1: 221. Also they are (respectively) like the prison, the punishment, the offence, the punisher, and the offender.
vsm2.14:221.2: And they are like the dish, the food, the curry sauce poured over the food, the server, and the eater.
vsm2.14:221.3: This is how the exposition should be known as to simile.
vsm2.14:222.1: 222. 5. Twice as to how to be seen: the exposition should be known twice as to how to be seen, namely, in brief and in detail.
vsm2.14:223.1:
223. In brief that is, collectively the five aggregates as objects of clinging should be seen as an enemy with drawn sword (S
IV 174) in the Snake Simile, as a burden (S III 25) according to the Burden Sutta, as a devourer (S III 87f) according to the
To-be-devoured Discourse, and as impermanent, painful, not-self, formed, and murderous, according to the Yamaka Sutta (S III 112f).
vsm2.14:224.1: 224. In detail that is, individually, matter should be regarded as a lump of froth because it will not stand squeezing,
vsm2.14:224.2: feeling as a bubble on water because it can only be enjoyed for an instant,
vsm2.14:224.3: perception as a mirage because it causes illusion,
vsm2.14:224.4: formations as a plantain trunk because they have no core,
vsm2.14:224.5: and consciousness as a conjuring trick because it deceives (S III 140–42).
vsm2.14:224.6: In particular, even sublime internal materiality should be regarded as foul (ugly);
vsm2.14:224.7: feeling should be regarded as painful because it is never free from the three kinds of suffering (see XVI.34);
vsm2.14:224.8: perception and formations as not-self because they are unmanageable;
vsm2.14:224.9: and consciousness as impermanent because it has the nature of rise and fall.
vsm2.14:225.1:
225. 6. As to good for one seeing thus: good comes to be accomplished in one who sees in the two ways
thus in brief and in detail. And the way of definition should be known according to that,
vsm2.14:225.2:
that is to say, firstly, one who sees the five aggregates as objects of clinging in the form
of an enemy with drawn sword, etc., is not worried by the aggregates,
vsm2.14:225.3: but one who sees materiality, etc., in detail as a lump of froth, etc., is not one who sees a core in the coreless.
vsm2.14:226.1:
226. And in particular, one who sees internal materiality as foul (ugly) fully
understands nutriment consisting of physical nutriment.
vsm2.14:226.2: He abandons the perversion of perceiving beauty in the foul (ugly),
vsm2.14:226.3:
he crosses the flood of sense desire, he is loosed from the bond of sense desire, he becomes canker-free as regards
the canker of sense desire, he breaks the bodily tie of covetousness. He does not cling with sense-desire clinging.
vsm2.14:227.1: 227. One who sees feeling as pain fully understands nutriment consisting of contact.
vsm2.14:227.2: He abandons the perversion of perceiving pleasure in the painful.
vsm2.14:227.3:
He crosses the flood of becoming. He is loosed from the bond of becoming. He becomes canker-free as regards
the canker of becoming. He breaks the bodily tie of ill will. He does not cling with rules-and-vows clinging.
vsm2.14:228.1: 228. One who sees perception and formations as not-self fully understands nutriment consisting of mental volition.
vsm2.14:228.2: He abandons the perversion of perceiving self in the not-self.
vsm2.14:228.3: He crosses the flood of views. He is loosed from the bond of views.
vsm2.14:228.4: He breaks the bodily tie of interpretations (insistence) that "This is the truth." He does not cling with self-theory clinging.
vsm2.14:229.1: 229. One who sees consciousness as impermanent fully understands nutriment consisting of consciousness.
vsm2.14:229.2: He abandons the perversion of perceiving permanence in the impermanent.
vsm2.14:229.3:
He crosses the flood of ignorance. He is loosed from the bond of ignorance.
He becomes canker-free as regards the canker of ignorance.
vsm2.14:229.4: He breaks the bodily tie of holding to rules and vows. He does not cling with false- view clinging.
vsm2.14:230.1:
230. Such blessings there will be From seeing them as murderers and otherwise,
Therefore the wise should see The aggregates as murderers and otherwise.
vsm2.14:230.2:
The fourteenth chapter called The Description of the Aggregates in the Treatise on the Development
of Understanding in the Path of Purification composed for the purpose of gladdening good people.
